messages:
mia: customer hit repeated 400s when calling our tool endpoint — runtime returns JSON schema validation error. attaching minimal payload and error.

mia: error from runtime: \"ValidationError: instance additionalProperties \n  Failed validating 'additionalProperties' in schema:\n    {\n      'additionalProperties': False,\n      'properties': {'args': {'type': 'object'}, 'name': {'type': 'string'}},\n      'required': ['name', 'args']\n    }\n  On instance:\n    {'name': 'embed', 'args': {'text': 'hello'}, 'session_id': 12345}\"

mia: payload they send (redacted):
```json
{
  "name": "embed",
  "args": { "text": "hello" },
  "session_id": 12345
}
```

cj: curious — are they using function-calling or tool_calling? session_id should be a string per our spec. looks like client app is sending number.

arjun: yep that number -> type mismatch + additionalProperties because our schema sets additionalProperties: false, and session_id not listed. two problems: (1) we expect session_id under args.session (server-side clients sometimes send it top-level), (2) type is wrong. quick repro with curl? ask customer to run this to see same error:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/toolcall \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"embed","args":{"text":"hi"},"session_id":12345}'
```

emily: can you paste the runtime schema that rejected this? i want to confirm whether session_id was intentionally excluded.

support-bot: uploaded file schema/toolcall-v1.json

arjun: snippet from schema/toolcall-v1.json:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "name": { "type": "string" },
    "args": { "type": "object" }
  },
  "required": ["name","args"],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

arjun: decision: customer used top-level session_id (not allowed) + numeric type. short-term workaround: tell them to move session_id under args.session as a string, e.g.:
```json
{"name":"embed","args":{"text":"hi","session":"s-12345"}}
```

mia: replied to customer with workaround + repro curl. also asked them to paste SDK version. they said using our python sdk 0.9.2.

cj: raise possiblity our python SDK 0.9.2 recently swizzled how session is serialized? @arjun can you search commit history for session serialization? if SDK is at fault we need rollback/patch.

arjun: quick check — sdk v0.9.2 had a change that added session to top-level for some convenience paths (PR #412). that explains it. the server schema never intended to accept top-level session_id. bug: SDK sent numeric IDs for sessions when callers passed int. patch options:
- change server schema to allow additionalProperties for backwards compat (risk: masking other issues)
- or patch SDK to keep session inside args and stringify session ids (preferable)

emily: prefer SDK patch + minor server tolerance. we'll add a regression test in runtime to reject additionalProperties but accept top-level session_id only if it matches string pattern? that seems messy.

mia: customer ok with SDK patch timeline (ETA 24h). i've escalated a ticket to eng-runtime and sdk team. ticket created: #SUP-3201.

arjun: plan: (1) hotfix sdk 0.9.3 that retains args.session and casts session ids to strings, (2) add a compatibility note in API docs, (3) add unit test in runtime to cover numeric-vs-string session scenarios, (4) consider small server-side tolerant check for top-level session_id for one release window.

cj: sounds good. assign owners and add timeline in ticket. ping me when patch published. :thumbsup:

emily: i'll add changelog line and test matrix entry. thanks team.

mia: closing thread — customer confirmed workaround works for now. will follow up after SDK patch.
